content: Diprobase is an emollient specifically designed for the management of eczema and dermatitis. It functions as an occlusive emollient, meaning it restores the protective oil layer on the skin's surface, which helps to reduce water loss from the skin. However, this property can make the treated area feel sticky after application. Diprobase does not contain any pharmacologically active ingredients. Its formulation consists of a combination of paraffins and water, along with cetomacrogol and cetostearyl alcohol, which act as emulsifying agents. It also includes chlorocresol, which serves as an antimicrobial preservative, as well as phosphoric acid and sodium dihydrogen phosphate. Dry skin occurs when the outermost layer of skin cells, known as the stratum corneum, lacks sufficient water. When this layer becomes dehydrated, it loses its flexibility, leading to cracking, scaling, and sometimes itching. The stratum corneum naturally contains water-holding substances that retain moisture from the deeper layers of the skin. Additionally, water is normally preserved in the stratum corneum by a surface film composed of natural oils (sebum) and broken-down skin cells, which slow the evaporation of water from the skin's surface. Diprobase works by enhancing this oil layer, thereby improving the skin's ability to retain moisture.
